_about: Astro Precise — the £7 Your Eclipse Edition. Honest template library. The engine computes WHERE the 12 Aug 2026 eclipse degree falls against a person's real natal chart; these templates turn that computed contact into words. TYPE LAW: the 'computed' line is fact (render in mono); the 'reflection' line is human meaning (render in warm serif). Everything traditional is framed as reflection, never prediction. Nothing here is fabricated — every number the engine drops in is real; the words only interpret it. Legal 'for reflection/entertainment' line ships with every reading.
voice: Calm, specific, grown-up. Fact first, then a gentle traditional meaning offered for reflection. No promises about health, money or love. No 'you will'. No fear.
legalLine: Astronomy is exact; the meaning is tradition, offered for reflection and entertainment — not advice or prediction.

reflectionFrames.conjunction: This eclipse falls right on {theme}. Eclipses have long been read as endings that clear a little space for a beginning — so this is a moment to notice what here feels ready to turn over.
reflectionFrames.opposition: This eclipse sits directly opposite {theme}. Tradition reads a facing like this as a call for balance — a nudge to see this part of you from the other side.
reflectionFrames.square: This eclipse presses on {theme}. A square is old shorthand for useful friction — the kind of tension that, handled gently, tends to move something that was stuck.
reflectionFrames.trine: This eclipse flows easily with {theme}. A trine is the kind, unforced contact — a good moment to lean on this strength rather than force anything.
reflectionFrames.sextile: This eclipse gently opens {theme}. A helpful angle is a small door, not a shove — an invitation you can take or leave.

overrides.sun|conjunction: This eclipse falls right on your Sun — your core sense of who you are. Of all the contacts, this is the personal one: a traditional marker of a chapter quietly closing so a truer one can begin. Held lightly, it is an invitation to ask what you have outgrown.
overrides.sun|opposition: This eclipse sits opposite your Sun. Tradition reads a facing like this as a mirror held up to identity — not a verdict, a chance to see how you look from the other side of the room.
overrides.sun|square: This eclipse squares your Sun. Old language calls that useful friction in the through-line of a life: something in how you recognise yourself is being asked to move, without anyone else having to notice.
overrides.moon|conjunction: This eclipse falls right on your Moon — your inner tides and what makes you feel safe. Tradition treats this as a tender, emotional reset; be a little gentler with yourself around it than you would think to be.
overrides.moon|opposition: This eclipse sits opposite your Moon. A facing here is often read as a conversation between what you need and what the world is asking — not a demand to choose, a chance to name both.
overrides.moon|square: This eclipse squares your Moon. The old shorthand is restlessness in the private rooms: habits of comfort that no longer quite fit, offered for noticing rather than for panic.
overrides.mercury|conjunction: This eclipse meets your Mercury — how you think, speak and sort the world. Tradition reads a conjunction here as a clean page in the notebook: a good moment to say the thing plainly, or to stop repeating a sentence that has finished.
overrides.mercury|opposition: This eclipse sits opposite your Mercury. A facing like this is often taken as a second opinion arriving — not to replace your own mind, but to let it hear itself from across the table.
overrides.mercury|square: This eclipse squares your Mercury. Useful friction in the talking and the thinking: a prompt to check which arguments you are still carrying out of habit.
overrides.venus|conjunction: This eclipse falls on your Venus — what you love, value and find beautiful. The traditional reading is a quiet audit of affection and taste: what is still yours, and what you have been keeping out of courtesy.
overrides.venus|opposition: This eclipse sits opposite your Venus. A mirror on the lovely and the valued — a chance to see the relationship, the taste, or the loyalty from the other side, without having to wreck it.
overrides.venus|square: This eclipse squares your Venus. Old language calls that a productive rub in matters of love and worth: something you care about is asking for a more honest arrangement.
overrides.mars|conjunction: This eclipse meets your Mars — drive, courage, the way you act. Tradition treats this as heat on the will: a moment to notice where effort is chosen and where it is only leftover momentum.
overrides.mars|opposition: This eclipse sits opposite your Mars. A facing here is often read as meeting your own force coming the other way — useful, if you let it show you how you push.
overrides.mars|square: This eclipse squares your Mars. Friction in the engine: the old reading is not a fight to pick, but a check on which battles still deserve you.
overrides.jupiter|conjunction: This eclipse falls on your Jupiter — growth, meaning, room to expand. Tradition reads a conjunction here as a wide door, not a guarantee: notice where you have been waiting for permission to take up space.
overrides.jupiter|opposition: This eclipse sits opposite your Jupiter. A facing on faith and appetite — a chance to see whether the big story you tell yourself still fits the life you are actually in.
overrides.jupiter|square: This eclipse squares your Jupiter. Useful tension in the wish to grow: the old shorthand is to ask which expansion is hunger, and which is habit.
overrides.saturn|conjunction: This eclipse meets your Saturn — your patience and your load. The old reading is not heavy: it is a moment to set down one thing you have been carrying out of habit rather than need.
overrides.saturn|opposition: This eclipse sits opposite your Saturn. A facing on duty and time — tradition offers it as a chance to see the structure from outside, and to keep only what still holds.
overrides.saturn|square: This eclipse squares your Saturn. Friction at the load-bearing wall: not a collapse, a prompt to check which rule you are still obeying after it has finished being useful.
overrides.uranus|conjunction: This eclipse meets your Uranus — the part that wants air and the unexpected. Tradition reads this as a crack in the routine: not a command to blow up your life, a notice that something wants more room.
overrides.uranus|opposition: This eclipse sits opposite your Uranus. A facing on freedom — a chance to see whether the rebellion you are still staging is current, or a costume from an earlier year.
overrides.uranus|square: This eclipse squares your Uranus. Useful static in the wish to break out: the old reading is to name the constraint honestly before you try to leave it.
overrides.neptune|conjunction: This eclipse falls on your Neptune — dreams, longing, the fog and the music. Tradition treats this as a thinning of the veil, which is also a warning to keep the facts in the other hand.
overrides.neptune|opposition: This eclipse sits opposite your Neptune. A facing on the ideal — a chance to see the dream from the street, and to keep it without letting it spend you.
overrides.neptune|square: This eclipse squares your Neptune. Friction between the vision and the day: old language offers it as a prompt to tell the longing from the leak.
overrides.pluto|conjunction: This eclipse meets your Pluto — what in you is quietly transforming. Tradition reads a conjunction here as a deep, slow turn: not theatre, a composting. Held lightly, it is permission to let one skin finish.
overrides.pluto|opposition: This eclipse sits opposite your Pluto. A facing on power and the under-storey — a chance to see the intensity from across the room instead of from inside it.
overrides.pluto|square: This eclipse squares your Pluto. Useful pressure on what is already changing: the old shorthand is not to force a crisis, but to stop pretending the old arrangement is still alive.
overrides.asc|conjunction: This eclipse falls right on your Ascendant — the face you meet the world with. It is read, traditionally, as a moment when how you show up is ready to shift; nobody else has to notice for it to be real.
overrides.asc|opposition: This eclipse sits opposite your Ascendant, which is also a conversation with the seventh-house other. Tradition reads a facing here as how you meet people meeting you back — a chance to notice the handshake, not to rewrite your face overnight.
overrides.asc|square: This eclipse squares your Ascendant. Friction in the way you begin and present: old language offers it as a check on whether the entrance still belongs to the person walking through it.
overrides.mc|conjunction: This eclipse falls on your career point — direction, work, the public path. Tradition reads a conjunction here as a chapter mark on the skyline, not a job-offer in the post. A good moment to ask whether the hill you are climbing is still the one you mean.
overrides.mc|opposition: This eclipse sits opposite your career point, facing the private ground of home and origin. The old reading is a balance between the public path and the room you come back to — neither has to win.
overrides.mc|square: This eclipse squares your career point. Useful friction in vocation and reputation: a prompt to notice which ambition is still chosen, and which is only being performed.

emptyState.computed: The eclipse point sits more than {maxOrb}° from every placement in your chart — no close contact for this eclipse.
emptyState.computedNoHard: No placement in your chart takes a direct hit from this eclipse: nothing of yours sits within {maxOrb}° of the eclipse point, or directly opposite it, or square to it.
emptyState.nearestSoft: There is a softer touch nearby — the eclipse point {frame} your {targetLabel}, {orbText} away. That contact is real; it is just a gentle one, and we would rather name it than build a night on it.
emptyState.nearestWide: The nearest contact of any kind is {orbText} from your {targetLabel} — real, and too wide to carry a night.
emptyState.reflection: So this one is quiet for you, and quiet is a real reading. Charts are not scored out of ten; the sky simply does not reach everybody on the same night, and plenty of places would happily sell you a reading anyway. You still get the record of the eclipse over your own town — and your chart is no less yours for sitting this one out.

perseid.computed: After the eclipse, the Perseids peaked overnight — the darkest window was roughly {darkStart}–{darkEnd}, radiant climbing in the north-east.
perseid.reflection: An old, unserious tradition worth keeping: the first shooting star you catch is yours to make a wish on.

shareLine: The eclipse landed {orbText} from my {targetLabel}. Check where it falls in yours →

questions.sun: So the question here is a quiet one: which version of you is asking to be lived openly now — and what have you outgrown?
questions.moon: So the question the sky hands you is not 'what should you want?' but the quieter one underneath: what do you actually need, before anyone told you what you were supposed to?
questions.mercury: So the question: what is waiting to be said plainly — and to whom?
questions.venus: So the question: what do you love that you have been treating as optional?
questions.mars: So the question: where is your effort going out of habit rather than choice?
questions.jupiter: So the question: where are you being invited to grow — and what small door have you not opened?
questions.saturn: So the question: which load are you carrying out of habit that was never yours to keep?
questions.uranus: So the question: where does your life ask for more room than you have given it?
questions.neptune: So the question: which dream have you been calling unrealistic mainly because it matters?
questions.pluto: So the question: what is quietly ending so something truer can take its place?
questions.asc: So the question: does the way you meet the world still fit the person doing the meeting?
questions.mc: So the question: is the direction you are walking still the one you would choose today?

close.computedPerseids: The same night, the Perseids peaked — up to {rate} meteors an hour after midnight, the radiant climbing in the north-east; the darkest window was roughly {darkStart}–{darkEnd}.
close.computedNoPerseids: After the eclipse the sky stayed busy. This plate is the keepable record of the contact.
close.serif: You do not have to answer any of this now. A page turned; you are allowed to simply keep the record of it.

secondary.serif: Quieter touches, worth a glance — the closest contact above is the one that carries the reading.

quietGate.note: UI RULE (binding): when quiet:true, the buyer must SEE the quiet verdict before paying — the empty state gates the sale, never surprises after it.
